title: Materialist Metaphysics
centralClaim: Reality is fundamentally physical; mental phenomena are ultimately reducible to physical processes.
whyItMatters: Offers a parsimonious explanation of existence, grounding experience in observable and measurable physical events. Challenges dualistic accounts by eliminating the need for non-physical substances or entities.

contributors.name: Thomas Hobbes
contributors.reason: Hobbes's materialism, emphasizing body and motion as the basis of reality, laid groundwork for later materialist philosophies.

contributors.name: J. J. C. Smart
contributors.reason: Smart's work in the philosophy of mind, particularly his identity theory, exemplifies contemporary materialism.

objections: The 'hard problem' of consciousness: Explaining subjective experience (qualia) solely in terms of physical processes remains a significant challenge.
Dualism: The persistence of dualistic arguments, suggesting the existence of non-physical mental states or substances.
Intentionality: How can purely physical systems possess intentionality – aboutness or directedness?
The problem of free will: If all events are causally determined by physical processes, how is genuine freedom possible?
